motion: Is secular humanism superior to Christianity at achieving human flourishing, rational decision-making, moral reasoning, and conflict resolution?

lockedRoutes.description: Establish secular humanism as more adept at advancing human flourishing through evidence-sensitive, revisable methods and practical comparison with Christian guidance.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: Show that human flourishing is the relevant shared goal and that secular methods yield more reliable decisions, moral guidance, learning, and conflict resolution than Christian methods.

motionBridge.description: Secular humanism is more adept than Christianity at achieving the motion's practical goals.

centralBridges.description: Relative evidence about shared human interests permits meaningful comparison without an ultimate standard.
Evidence-sensitive and revisable inquiry produces transferable knowledge and improved practical outcomes.
Autonomy, equality, consequences, and human interests provide better moral guidance than scriptural authority.
Public evidence resolves disagreement more reliably than competing claims of revelation or interpretation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Using shared logical axioms does not require adding an unsupported divine explanation.
The capacity to revise goals and methods in light of outcomes improves error correction.

lockedRoutes.description: Defeat the claimed superiority by arguing that secular humanism lacks non-arbitrary foundations for rational inference, science, and ethics while Christianity supplies them.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: Show that secular humanism cannot justify the standards and cognitive tools its comparison requires, and that Christian revelation and God's character provide a coherent superior foundation.

motionBridge.description: Secular humanism cannot be superior because its foundational commitments undermine its own claims.

centralBridges.description: A valid superiority comparison requires a non-arbitrary standard applicable across both worldviews.
Naturalistic physical processes cannot adequately justify trustworthy logical inference.
Secular humanism cannot justify the logical and inductive presuppositions required by science.
Consequentialist human-flourishing ethics lacks an objective standard and becomes circular or permissive.

subsidiaryBridges.description: God's invariant character and revelation ground logic, natural regularity, and moral norms.
Christian disagreements over nonessentials do not defeat shared essential doctrines or New Testament ethics.

lockedSections.title: The standard for superiority
lockedSections.rationale: The parties contest whether relative facts about a shared goal suffice or whether comparison requires a worldview-neutral objective foundation.

proMoves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
proMoves.proposition: Reasonably warranted beliefs and non-subjective facts permit relative comparisons of methods without absolute certainty or an ultimate measuring standard.

sourceSpan.excerpt: absolute certainty isn't relevant to this discussion... the facts of reality, which... are non-subjective and universal, can dictate which methods are superior. Relative comparisons are all that is needed.

conMoves.speaker: Matt Slick
conMoves.proposition: A worldview that is self-refuting cannot be superior, so secular humanism must first provide coherent foundations for knowledge and rationality.

sourceSpan.excerpt: one philosophical position cannot be superior to another... if that philosophical position is self-refuting... that which is self-refuting is automatically inferior to that which is not self-refuting.

lockedSections.title: Empirical method, learning, and science
lockedSections.rationale: The core practical comparison pits secular humanism's revisable empirical learning against the objection that science cannot justify its own logical and inductive presuppositions.

proMoves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
proMoves.proposition: Secular humanism improves flourishing by testing outcomes, learning transferable methods, and revising its goals and practices when evidence changes.

sourceSpan.excerpt: medical treatments... foster a better understanding and lead to improvements in human flourishing... the secular process is better because we learn more from it... It is revisible. It can change its positions and it can change its goals.

conMoves.speaker: Matt Slick
conMoves.proposition: Secular reliance on science cannot justify the laws of logic or uniformity of nature that scientific inference itself presupposes, whereas Christianity can ground them in God.

sourceSpan.excerpt: the scientific method is based on philosophical assumptions... assumes the validity of the laws of logic... science presupposes the regularity of nature... Christianity... can trust that the universe is made in a consistent and predictable manner.

lockedSections.title: Moral standards and practical guidance
lockedSections.rationale: The ethical dispute concerns whether autonomy, equality, harm, and consequences provide corrigible guidance or collapse into an arbitrary circular standard.

proMoves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
proMoves.proposition: Starting from equality, autonomy, cooperation, and flourishing rules out slavery and murder while supplying practical reasons for peaceful conduct.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Isn't it enough to work for peace in the life that we have now?... when you begin with a foundation of equality and autonomy... Slavery and murder are done from the outset... We talked about equality.

conMoves.speaker: Matt Slick
conMoves.proposition: Consequentialist ethics cannot non-circularly establish that reducing harm is good and may fail to condemn intrinsically wrongful acts when no detectable harm occurs.

sourceSpan.excerpt: secular humanists hold that ethics is consequential to be judged by results... How do we know that the reduction of harm is good?... You have to appeal to the very act that is wrong by nature, and that refutes consequentialism.

lockedSections.title: Revelation, disagreement, and Christian guidance
lockedSections.rationale: The parties dispute whether Christian interpretive disagreement disables practical guidance or concerns only nonessential details within a stable revealed framework.

proMoves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
proMoves.proposition: Expert Christians can use the same scriptures to support incompatible salvation accounts, showing that revelation lacks a reliable conflict-resolution method.

sourceSpan.excerpt: two people who both believe they're Christians are pointing to the same book... confirm mutually exclusive contradictory positions... They both think they have a method to reach the truth and they reach mutually exclusive contradictory positions.

conMoves.speaker: Matt Slick
conMoves.proposition: The disputed salvation order is nonessential because both Christians affirm salvation by grace through faith in Christ, while current Christian ethics is codified in New Testament revelation.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Jesse Morrell and I both believe that salvation is by grace alone, through faith alone, and Christ alone... the differences of our opinions are... non-essential... Christian principles today, found in the New Testament.

lockedSections.title: Naturalistic reason and divine grounding
lockedSections.rationale: The most sustained exchange asks whether physical cognition is self-defeating and whether adding God explains logic better than shared axiomatic presuppositions.

proMoves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
proMoves.proposition: Secular humanism may presuppose logic without self-refutation because both sides share those axioms, while the further claim that God accounts for them remains undemonstrated.

sourceSpan.excerpt: secular humanism doesn't claim that it can account for the laws of logic. So it's not self-refuting... presuppositionalists... never demonstrate... my worldview accounts for this because God... we agree on the foundations of logic.

conMoves.speaker: Matt Slick
conMoves.proposition: If cognition consists only of physical chemical reactions, secular humanism cannot justify trusting its logical conclusions and therefore undermines belief in itself.

sourceSpan.excerpt: it's still a set of chemicals... how do you justify... that your logical inferences in your brain could be trusted?... you couldn't even know if secular humanism is true... It refutes itself.
